card.title: Exam bank — every board question on curved mirrors

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Two questions: why object-at-F images at infinity (2023: parallel reflected beam) and the 30 cm object with f = 10 cm numerical (2022: image at 15 cm, halved, inverted, real). Real images meet on screen; virtual images meet only in apparent extension.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u · f = R/2 · m = -v/u (minus = inverted real, plus = erect virtual)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Paraxial rays only (meaning wide beams blur via spherical aberration). Cartesian signs fixed once (incident light left to right). Focus-at-F logic needs the concave geometry (parallel beam definition of focus).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Object at C images at C same-size inverted. Object inside F gives erect magnified virtual behind mirror. Convex always gives virtual erect diminished between P and F. At F: 1/v = 0, so v = infinity.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: NEB 2022 (4): u = -30, f = -10 gives 1/v = -1/10 + 1/30 = -2/30, so v = -15 cm; m = -(-15)/(-30) = -0.5 (real, inverted, halved). NEB 2023 (3): at F every reflected ray parallels the axis (focus definition), hence meeting at infinity.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Mark-losers: sign mixing between conventions; real confused with virtual (screen test decides); formula applied to wide-aperture mirrors. Brightness and aberration sit outside the formula.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Similar triangles (object/pole and focus pairs) give v/u = (v-f)/f, dividing to 1/f = 1/v + 1/u. Six object positions memorised as image map (infinity-to-F through P-to-F) answer every ray question.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Signs first (Cartesian), numbers second. Real means negative m; virtual positive. 'At F' always means parallel out, image at infinity.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2023 (3): object at F plus object at C behaviour. NEB 2022 (4): 30 cm/f10 numerical with nature. That is the complete bank.
